title: DVR localizations at associated primes of reduced quotients of flat Noetherian algebras
statement: Let R and A be commutative Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] with A an R-algebra flat as an R-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Let p be a prime ideal of R whose localization R_p [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a discrete valuation ring. Suppose A/pA is reduced. Let q be a prime ideal of A which is the annihilator of an element z of A/pA [def-weil-pbc-annihilator-associated-primes]. Then A_q is an integral domain and a discrete valuation ring. Here pA is the image of p under R -> A, and reduced means that every nilpotent element is zero. No local-ring or completion hypothesis on R or A is required.

source.place: Tag 032Z, algebraic argument after reducedness; generalization from the completion to a flat Noetherian algebra, written out by G2; source verified at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/032Z

proof.text: Set B=A/pA and C=A_q, and write q=Ann(z). Properness forces z nonzero. Lift z to a in A. If a belonged to q, then z squared would vanish, contrary to reducedness. Since pA kills B, pA<=q. For b in q, ba belongs to pA. The image of a in C is a unit, so cancelling it shows qC=pC. Lean proves this directly with the colon ideal, the quotient map and localization units in the private helpers quotient_annihilator_le and associated_quotient_map_eq.

For r outside p, its image in the domain R/p is nonzero and regular. Flat base change makes (R/p) tensor_R A flat over R/p, so scalar multiplication by this image is injective. The canonical tensor-quotient equivalence identifies this tensor product with B. Thus r cannot annihilate the nonzero element z. Together with pA<=q this shows q contracts to p. Lean uses Algebra.TensorProduct.quotIdealMapEquivQuotTensor and Module.Flat.isSMulRegular_of_isRegular in associated_quotient_comap.

Since q contracts to p, equip C with its canonical R_p-algebra structure. Localization and composition preserve flatness, so C is flat over R_p (the Mathlib instance in RingTheory/Flat/Localization.lean). The scalar tower and ideal-map composition identities identify the extension of the maximal ideal of R_p with pC=qC, the maximal ideal of C. Choose an irreducible uniformizer x of the DVR R_p. Its image y in C generates the maximal ideal. As x is nonzero in the domain R_p, flatness makes multiplication by y injective. This transfers a regular maximal-ideal generator without choosing a numerator in R or clearing denominators.

C is Noetherian by localization and local at q. Krull intersection gives intersection_n m_C^n=0. For nonzero b choose N with b outside m_C^N. Induction on N gives b=y^n*u with u a unit: a nonunit lies in (y), so b=y*c, and c must be outside m_C^(N-1). With y regular, y^n*(u*c)=0 forces c=0. Thus products of nonzero elements are nonzero, giving IsDomain C. Regularity and nontriviality show y is nonzero; since (y)=m_C, y is irreducible. The unit-times-power factorization criterion IsDiscreteValuationRing.ofHasUnitMulPowIrreducibleFactorization then gives the DVR structure. The private helpers factor_of_bound, factor_nonzero and dvr_of_regular_maximal_generator carry this argument.

proof_origin.place: Tag 032Z, algebraic argument after reducedness, checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/032Z; F2 uses the induced flat local map R_p -> A_q to transfer a uniformizer, and proves the final Krull-intersection factorization in Lean. The factorization proof also follows the completed private arguments in Sheaf.RingTheory.CohenCompletionDVR; no import of that module is needed.

from.place: The codimension-one analytically-unramified completion argument in step 4: its algebraic part after completion Noetherianity, flatness and reducedness

lean.statement:
theorem isDiscreteValuationRing_atPrime_of_flat_reduced_quotient
    (R : Type u) (A : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing A] [Module.Flat R A]
    (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] [IsDomain (Localization.AtPrime p)]
    [IsDiscreteValuationRing (Localization.AtPrime p)]
    [IsReduced (A ⧸ p.map (algebraMap R A))]
    (q : Ideal A) [q.IsPrime]
    (hq : ∃ z : A ⧸ p.map (algebraMap R A),
      q = (⊥ : Submodule A (A ⧸ p.map (algebraMap R A))).colon {z}) :
    ∃ (_ : IsDomain (Localization.AtPrime q)),
      IsDiscreteValuationRing (Localization.AtPrime q)
